chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Abū ʿAlī al-Ashʿarī, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Abū Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, concerning a man who performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah for eight circuits—what is upon him? So he said:
If it was done by mistake, he should disregard one and count seven.

key_terms.بِسَبْعَةٍ: as seven circuits, the required number for saʿy
key_terms.طَرَحَ: he disregarded or dropped from consideration
key_terms.وَاعْتَدَّ: he counted or reckoned as valid

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs eight circuits of saʿy by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who performs eight circuits in saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah instead of seven. If the addition occurred by mistake, one circuit is to be disregarded and the saʿy is counted as seven.
